text:
Fabian Zetterlund is doing a lot of things right for Ottawa and not much of it shows up on the scoresheet. The Senators have 64% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, 16 points better than when he sits, one of the best relative marks on the team.

The finish is what's missing. He has two goals on 4.4 expected, shooting 5.3% against a normal range of 10 to 15%. One of them came on the power play Saturday against Utah. Goals tend to follow chances, and he keeps getting them.

His role just changed too. With William Eklund on injured reserve, Tim Stützle has moved onto his line with Dylan Cozens, and his ice time is up almost two minutes over the last ten games. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on only 33% of his entries, a dump-and-chase player, which fits next to Stützle's speed. Our projection sees about 17 goals.
